questions.explanation: Programs received 10 percent of $1,500,000 in 2024, which is $150,000. Raising it by 60 percent gives 1.6 * 150,000 = $240,000. The other four categories keep their 2024 amounts, which total 1,500,000 - 150,000 = $1,350,000, so the 2025 budget is 1,350,000 + 240,000 = $1,590,000. Programs' share is 240,000/1,590,000 = 0.1509, which rounds to 15 percent.
questions.trap: Multiplying the 10 percent share directly by 1.6 gives 16 percent. That treats the total budget as fixed, but the extra $90,000 also enlarges the denominator, so the true share is 15 percent, not 16 percent.

questions.question:
The bar graph shows the average (arithmetic mean) score on a certification exam at each of four testing centers. The value n printed below each bar is the number of candidates who took the exam at that center. Every one of the 200 candidates took the exam at exactly one of the four centers.

What is the average (arithmetic mean) score of all 200 candidates?
questions.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 480 320" width="480" height="320" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><text x="240" y="22" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="13" fill="#1f2937">Average Certification Exam Score by Testing Centre</text><path d="M62 242H458M62 204H458M62 166H458M62 128H458M62 90H458M62 52H458" stroke="#1f2937" stroke-width="0.5" fill="none"/><g stroke="#1f2937" stroke-width="2" fill="#e5edf7"><rect x="89" y="67.2" width="58" height="174.8"/><rect x="173" y="82.4" width="58" height="159.6"/><rect x="257" y="97.6" width="58" height="144.4"/><rect x="341" y="120.4" width="58" height="121.6"/></g><path d="M62 52V242 H458" stroke="#1f2937" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><g font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="12" fill="#1f2937"><text x="56" y="246" text-anchor="end">0</text><text x="56" y="208" text-anchor="end">20</text><text x="56" y="170" text-anchor="end">40</text><text x="56" y="132" text-anchor="end">60</text><text x="56" y="94" text-anchor="end">80</text><text x="56" y="56" text-anchor="end">100</text><text x="118" y="61.2" text-anchor="middle">92</text><text x="118" y="260" text-anchor="middle">Alder</text><text x="118" y="276" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11">n = 20</text><text x="202" y="76.4" text-anchor="middle">84</text><text x="202" y="260" text-anchor="middle">Birch</text><text x="202" y="276" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11">n = 30</text><text x="286" y="91.6" text-anchor="middle">76</text><text x="286" y="260" text-anchor="middle">Cedar</text><text x="286" y="276" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11">n = 50</text><text x="370" y="114.4" text-anchor="middle">64</text><text x="370" y="260" text-anchor="middle">Dorn</text><text x="370" y="276" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11">n = 100</text><text x="260" y="300" text-anchor="middle">Testing centre (n = number of candidates)</text><text transform="rotate(-90 16 150)" x="16" y="150" text-anchor="middle">Average score (points)</text></g></svg>
questions.explanation: Because the centers hold different numbers of candidates, the overall mean is a weighted mean. Total points scored: Alder 20 * 92 = 1,840; Birch 30 * 84 = 2,520; Cedar 50 * 76 = 3,800; Dorn 100 * 64 = 6,400. The sum is 14,560 points over 200 candidates, so the mean is 14,560/200 = 72.8.
questions.trap: Averaging the four bar heights gives (92 + 84 + 76 + 64)/4 = 79.0, choice C. That treats the four centers as equally sized, but Dorn alone holds half of all candidates and pulls the true mean well below 79.

questions.question:
The bar graph shows the average (arithmetic mean) score on a certification exam at each of four testing centers. The value n printed below each bar is the number of candidates who took the exam at that center. Every one of the 200 candidates took the exam at exactly one of the four centers.

Quantity A: The total number of points scored by all candidates at Dorn
Quantity B: The total number of points scored by all candidates at Alder, Birch and Cedar combined

options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation: A center's total points equal its average score times its number of candidates. Quantity A: Dorn contributes 100 * 64 = 6,400 points. Quantity B: Alder 20 * 92 = 1,840, Birch 30 * 84 = 2,520 and Cedar 50 * 76 = 3,800, for a combined 8,160 points. Since 8,160 is greater than 6,400, Quantity B is greater.
questions.trap: Dorn's 100 candidates exactly match the 20 + 30 + 50 = 100 candidates at the other three centers, so a student who compares only the head counts concludes the totals are equal and picks C. Equal group sizes do not give equal point totals when the averages differ.

questions.question:
The bar graph shows the average (arithmetic mean) score on a certification exam at each of four testing centers. The value n printed below each bar is the number of candidates who took the exam at that center. Every one of the 200 candidates took the exam at exactly one of the four centers.

Which of the following statements are true?

Indicate all such statements.
questions.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 480 320" width="480" height="320" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><text x="240" y="22" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="13" fill="#1f2937">Average Certification Exam Score by Testing Centre</text><path d="M62 242H458M62 204H458M62 166H458M62 128H458M62 90H458M62 52H458" stroke="#1f2937" stroke-width="0.5" fill="none"/><g stroke="#1f2937" stroke-width="2" fill="#e5edf7"><rect x="89" y="67.2" width="58" height="174.8"/><rect x="173" y="82.4" width="58" height="159.6"/><rect x="257" y="97.6" width="58" height="144.4"/><rect x="341" y="120.4" width="58" height="121.6"/></g><path d="M62 52V242 H458" stroke="#1f2937" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><g font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="12" fill="#1f2937"><text x="56" y="246" text-anchor="end">0</text><text x="56" y="208" text-anchor="end">20</text><text x="56" y="170" text-anchor="end">40</text><text x="56" y="132" text-anchor="end">60</text><text x="56" y="94" text-anchor="end">80</text><text x="56" y="56" text-anchor="end">100</text><text x="118" y="61.2" text-anchor="middle">92</text><text x="118" y="260" text-anchor="middle">Alder</text><text x="118" y="276" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11">n = 20</text><text x="202" y="76.4" text-anchor="middle">84</text><text x="202" y="260" text-anchor="middle">Birch</text><text x="202" y="276" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11">n = 30</text><text x="286" y="91.6" text-anchor="middle">76</text><text x="286" y="260" text-anchor="middle">Cedar</text><text x="286" y="276" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11">n = 50</text><text x="370" y="114.4" text-anchor="middle">64</text><text x="370" y="260" text-anchor="middle">Dorn</text><text x="370" y="276" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11">n = 100</text><text x="260" y="300" text-anchor="middle">Testing centre (n = number of candidates)</text><text transform="rotate(-90 16 150)" x="16" y="150" text-anchor="middle">Average score (points)</text></g></svg>
options: A. The average score of all 200 candidates was less than 75.
B. The combined number of candidates at Alder and Birch was greater than the number of candidates at Dorn.
C. The combined average score of the candidates at Alder and Birch exceeded the combined average score of the candidates at Cedar and Dorn by more than 18 points.
D. The number of candidates at Dorn was more than 3 times the number of candidates at Birch.
E. The average score at Birch was 20 percent greater than the average score at Dorn.
F. The average score of all 200 candidates was greater than the median of the four centre averages.
questions.explanation: The weighted totals are Alder 1,840, Birch 2,520, Cedar 3,800 and Dorn 6,400, summing to 14,560 points over 200 candidates. A: the overall mean is 14,560/200 = 72.8, which is less than 75, so A is true. B: Alder and Birch hold 20 + 30 = 50 candidates against Dorn's 100, so B is false. C: Alder and Birch average (1,840 + 2,520)/50 = 87.2 while Cedar and Dorn average (3,800 + 6,400)/150 = 68.0, a gap of 19.2 points, which exceeds 18, so C is true. A student who ignores the candidate counts and averages the bar heights instead gets 88 against 70, a gap of exactly 18, which does not exceed 18 - so this option separates the weighted method from the unweighted one. D: 3 * 30 = 90 and Dorn has 100 candidates, so D is true. E: (84 - 64)/64 = 31.25 percent, not 20 percent, so E is false. F: the median of 92, 84, 76 and 64 is (84 + 76)/2 = 80, and 72.8 is less than 80, so F is false.
questions.trap: Statement E catches students who subtract the bar heights, get 84 - 64 = 20, and read that gap of 20 points as '20 percent greater'. A percent comparison divides by the base, and 20/64 = 31.25 percent, so E must be left unselected.
